title: 2024 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults
organization: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology

diagnosis.content: HTN is defined as BP ≥130/80 mmHg. Confirm with multiple readings over time or ambulatory BP monitoring.
key_points: Use home BP monitoring for confirmation

treatment.content: First-line therapy for HTN includes ACE inhibitors, ARBs, CCBs, or thiazide diuretics. Choice depends on comorbidities.
key_points: ACE-I/ARB: First-line for HTN with diabetes, CKD, or proteinuria
CCB: Alternative first-line, good for elderly and African Americans
Beta-blockers: Second-line unless specific indication (CAD, HF)

special_populations.diabetes: ACE-I or ARB preferred. Target BP <130/80 mmHg
special_populations.ckd: ACE-I or ARB if proteinuria present. Monitor K+ and Cr
special_populations.elderly: Consider lower starting doses. CCB often well-tolerated

monitoring.content: Monitor BP response, adherence, and adverse effects. Adjust therapy as needed.
key_points: Recheck BP in 1 month after initiation
Monitor renal function and electrolytes with ACE-I/ARB
Assess for orthostatic hypotension in elderly

drug-dosing.content: Start at standard doses unless specific contraindications. Titrate to achieve target BP.

examples.lisinopril: Start 10mg daily, max 40mg daily. Reduce dose if eGFR <30
examples.amlodipine: Start 5mg daily, max 10mg daily. No renal adjustment needed
